People who lack myophosphorylase , a glycolytic enzyme responsible for breaking down glycogen and thus inducing lactate production, demonstrate an attenuated post-exercise growth hormone response (87), providing strong evidence for a link between lactate production and GH release. A metabolite-induced decrease in pH also may augment GH release via chemoreflex stimulation regulated by intramuscular metaboreceptors and group III and IV afferents (154, 291).
